$comment: Allowlist and denylist for the Debloat Center.
verdict 'safe'     — Microsoft ships it and the Store can put it back.
verdict 'keep'     — removal is possible but something you will notice.
verdict 'protected' — Novimize will not offer it, with the reason.
Anything not listed here is 'unknown': it is still removable, but the
dialog says so rather than implying the entry was reviewed. Framework
packages, packages Windows marks NonRemovable, and packages something
else is waiting on are refused by the engine regardless of this file —
this file is an opinion, the dependency graph is a fact.

entries.reason: Without the Store, nothing removed here can be put back from it.
The Start menu itself.
The shell layer every window and the taskbar sit on.
Windows Search. Removing it takes the search box and indexed files with it.
Wired into Search and the Start menu on builds that still ship it.
The Windows Security interface — the only way to see Defender's state.
Settings. Nothing else can change what Settings changes.
Microsoft account sign-in broker. Accounts stop authenticating.
Account settings and credential UI.
The lock screen.
The OOBE and account experience host.
Delivers the Start menu's app suggestions — turning those off is a Settings toggle, not a removal.
Cortana. Removed on every build Microsoft has retired it from.
The News widget. Nothing else reads it.
Weather app. The taskbar widget has its own copy.
Opens a support page; a browser does the same.
'Get Started' tips app.
3D Viewer.
Office promotional hub, not Office itself.
Solitaire.
Sticky Notes. Its notes sync to the account, so signing in again brings them back.
Mixed Reality Portal. Meaningful only with a headset.
Contacts app. Mail and Outlook keep their own.
Skype. Standalone installer exists if you want it back.
Alarms and Clock.
Feedback Hub.
Maps.
Sound Recorder.
Phone Link. The mobile app reconnects when you reinstall it.
Media Player (the Zune successor).
Films & TV.
Power Automate desktop. Not used unless you built flows.
Quick Assist remote support.
Clipchamp video editor.
OneNote for Windows 10. The Store copy is separate.
New Teams. Removing it signs you out of every organisation you joined through it.
The new Outlook. If your mail lives here, removal takes it with the account setup.
Dev Home. Widgets and terminal integration disappear with it.
Xbox app. Game Pass, social and controller config live here.
Game Bar. The screenshot and recording shortcuts stop working.
Xbox sign-in. Games that use a Microsoft account will not connect.
The Xbox sign-in UI other Xbox packages call.
Windows Terminal — the default console on a fresh profile.
Paint. The snipping tool hands screenshots to it.
Snipping Tool. Win+Shift+S stops working without it.
Calculator. Nothing depends on it, but nothing replaces it either.
